policy_title: Improve Climate Resilience and Protect Nature
stated: Labour will improve resilience and preparation across government and emergency services for climate impacts like flooding and coastal erosion. They will also deliver Environment Act targets, create nine new National River Walks and three new National Forests, plant millions of trees, and expand nature-rich habitats. The party is committed to a circular economy to reduce waste.

source.quote: Labour will improve resilience and preparation across central government, local authorities, local communities, and emergency services. This includes formally working with all stakeholders in the Fire and Rescue services to inform policy and establish national standards. Labour will deliver for nature, taking action to meet our Environment Act targets, and will work in partnership with civil society, communities and business to restore and protect our natural world. As part of our plans to improve responsible access to nature, Labour will create nine new National River Walks, one in each region of England, and establish three new National Forests in England, whilst planting millions of trees and creating new woodlands. Labour will expand nature-rich habitats such as wetlands, peat bogs and forests so families can explore and wildlife can thrive, including on public land. Labour is committed to reducing waste by moving to a circular economy.

bearing_set.reason: Directly targets emissions resilience, habitat expansion, water/nature quality, and climate adaptation — all core O6 indicators.

Explicitly improving government and emergency-service resilience to flooding and coastal erosion directly moves the 'resilience to external threats' indicator and reduces harm (deaths, displacement) from climate hazard events.

Improved flood and coastal-erosion resilience directly protects economic infrastructure, housing stock, and livelihoods from climate damage; near-term investment costs versus long-term avoided losses from flooding (UK Environment Agency estimated £1bn+ annual flood damage) constitutes a real dual-horizon productivity and living-standards verdict.

membership_note: Two genuine bearings: O6 is the primary design target; O13 earns a real verdict via the concrete mechanism of protected economic infrastructure and avoided flood-damage costs. Other fundamentals (O5, O12, O15) were considered but do not clear the non-negligible bar: flood preparedness does not fit O5's crime/security indicators; the policy specifies no unfunded cost quantum that would materially move O12 on its own; and green-space cohesion effects on O15 are too diffuse and indirect to mechanistically justify inclusion.
